comments.author: @jacoblodzinski651
comments.text: Former Alaskan here, to put it lightly, there's a bug in Alaska, and it bites you as soon as you step foot on Alaska. This bug is invisible, and you don't feel it bite, but once it does you become addicted to the sheer raw beauty of Alaska. I lived on Kenai lake outside of moose pass, and even closer to Ptarmigan creek, right next to Victor creek. There's a trail directly across from my house that goes straight into the mountains, and it brings you to treeline where it opens up into the most beautiful mountain valley. It doesn't matter what you do, where you go, or what kind of adventure you want to have, because Alaska the great will show you an experience you will remember for the rest of your life. I tell this to anyone who asks, if youve got some extra money, some extra time, and a window of opportunity, don't think about it- JUST GO! Buy the ticket, rent a camper, and just go explore, theres hundreds of parks, trails, and campsites dotted along each highway. You can literally just pick and choose as you go along, or do the due diligence and plan a specific fishing or hunting trip, maybe you want to go hunt for gold with your family! The possibilities are endless and Alaska is your oyster, not to mention the wild oysters from Alaskas pristine waters are delicious! Go visit the sealife center, or maybe drive to Mt McKinley,  The brooks range 1:03:02 is also incredibly beautiful, but it's far north, I've been there 4 times on hunting trips but the beauty is raw and severe, it will make your jaw drop. Climb a mountain, catch a salmon or maybe a Halibut. I cannot express to you enough how actually beautiful Alaska is. Go get bit by the bug 😉
